sources.quote: The audit identified ~64,000 documents that were temporarily removed from the DOJ website after the initial public release, as well as ~24,000 documents with post-release size changes suggesting modification.
sources.searcher_note: Independent audit of the DOJ Epstein Library (Feb-Mar 2026) on removed/changed documents inside data sets 1-12. No mention of data sets 13+ or 403/404 pages.

sources.quote: Today's production marks the Department's compliance with its production obligations under the Act.
sources.searcher_note: DOJ letter accompanying data sets 9-12: says production under the Epstein Files Transparency Act is complete (over 3 million pages; 6 million identified; ~200,000 withheld or redacted for privilege). Sits against any reading that further data sets were built for release. PDF.

notes: No source found that mentions data sets 13-40, 403/'access denied' or 404/'not found' responses on the DOJ Epstein site, a March 11 2026 probe, or data set 9 being visible before its Jan 30 release. Search summaries' 'Access Denied' hits refer to the site's 18+ age gate, not data-set pages. Live DOJ Disclosures page (justice.gov/epstein/doj-disclosures), fetched 2026-09-25, lists only Data Set 1 through Data Set 12 and letters dated Dec 19 2025, Jan 30 2026 and Feb 14 2026; Wikipedia's Epstein files article ends its chronology with the March 5 2026 re-release of ~50,000 previously removed files. Post-cutoff coverage found (Courthouse News 2026-08-13, Axios/CBS June-July 2026) is about redaction fights in the Phang lawsuit before Judge Sullivan, not about new data sets. Medium technical guide (erenozkaradeniz) returned 403; Harvard tagteam repost 'The Epstein Files Trump's DOJ Didn't Mean to Show You' returned 503.
